decision: Does TensorLBM adopt openLBMPM's shared-memory warp-shift streaming (row-tile staging in shared memory + one-lane modular shift + in-place cross-tile repair + direct neighbour-row delivery for the vertical half of the stencil) as a backend streaming kernel? D1 adopt as-is / D2 adopt the rule with the two domain wraps closed and keep the periodic whole-array pull as the CPU reference / D3 reject.
alternatives: A1_oss_transplant: warp_shift_stream, upstream rule (tile = 32 = warp), vectorised form, upstream edge behaviour preserved (x_periodic=y_periodic=False)
A2_transplant_fixed: same rule with both domain wraps closed (x_periodic=y_periodic=True) -- the only mode comparable to a periodic reference flow
A3_repo_reference: in-repo periodic pull streaming (torch.roll over the whole (9,ny,nx) field) -- identical BGK collision, identical equilibrium
hypothesis: H1 (semantic identity): the vectorised warpshift equals the line-by-line upstream transcription bit for bit (max |df| = 0, threshold 1e-12). H2 (physics neutrality): with both wraps closed the operator equals the pull reference bit for bit and the Taylor-Green decay rate it produces is inside the owner 15 % band. H3 (defect of the verbatim kernel): without the two wraps the domain edge columns/rows are inconsistent, which shows up as mass drift and a large decay-rate error -- i.e. the as-is transplant (D1) must be rejected. H0 falsifiers: any KPI outside its predeclared threshold.

metrics.K1_max_abs_diff: max |warp_shift_stream - oss_literal_stream| over the whole (9,ny,nx) field, random field + TG field, tiles 8/16/32
metrics.K1_bitwise: torch.equal(...) (exact equality of the two double tensors)
metrics.K2_max_abs_diff: max |warp_shift_stream(periodic) - pull_stream| , single step and after 200 coupled BGK steps
metrics.K3_decay_rel_err: |lambda_measured - lambda_analytic| / lambda_analytic where E(t) = E0 exp(-2 lambda t), lambda = nu k^2, k = 2 pi / L, measured from kinetic energy over 800 steps
metrics.K4_verbatim_defect: for the as-is kernel: relative mass drift |sum f - sum f0| / sum f0 over 100 steps, and K3 decay relative error on the same run
metrics.K5_mlups: nx*ny*steps / elapsed / 1e6 (million lattice-site updates per second), single CPU process, float64, per streaming backend and tile width

unit_of_analysis: one streaming invocation (K1/K2) or one completed Taylor-Green run at fixed (L, u0, tau, steps) (K3/K4) or one timing repetition (K5)

baseline_control.semantic_baseline: oss_literal_stream: line-by-line transcription of calStreamingGPU + exchangeDistrGlobalGPU including the upstream guards; this is the OSS arm (the CUDA kernel cannot be executed here, no GPU: torch.cuda.is_available() == False)
baseline_control.physical_baseline: analytic Taylor-Green decay E(t) = E0 exp(-2 nu k^2 t) of the D2Q9 BGK model in the incompressible limit
baseline_control.representation_control: A3 pull_stream shares collision, equilibrium, domain, dtype and step count with A1/A2; the only changed variable is the streaming operator
baseline_control.note: the upstream OSS binary is not executed (needs CUDA + its own Shan-Chen multiphase driver); the OSS arm is a semantics-exact transcription, recorded as a comparison limit and not silently upgraded

predeclared_thresholds.K5_verdict_rule: adopt the tile kernel for the CPU backend only if it is at least as fast as the pull reference (>= 1.0x MLUPS) at some tile width; otherwise record the recipe as a GPU-backend candidate
predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: K1/K2 are identity checks (machine precision). K3 uses the owner 15 % band; no case is dropped or trimmed after seeing results.

stopping_rule: fixed design: K1/K2 on tiles {8,16,32} and fields {random(nx=96,ny=40), TG(L=64)}; K3 on the full grid L in {64,128,256} x u0 in {0.02,0.04,0.08} with tau=0.8 and 800 steps each; K4 one run (L=64, u0=0.04, 100 steps); K5 three timing repetitions per arm on 128^2 and 256^2, median reported. No arm added or removed after inspecting KPIs; wall-clock budget 1200 s (actual run below).
variables_changed: streaming backend: A1 as-is warp shift / A2 wraparound warp shift / A3 pull
variables_held_fixed: BGK collision and equilibrium (tensorlbm.d2q9.equilibrium, float64 exact weights)
step count 800 for K3, 100 for K4, single CPU process
confounders: no GPU in this environment: the warp-shift concept exists for shared-memory speed, the CPU emulation may be slower than the pull reference for reasons unrelated to the algorithm (extra staged copy) -- K5 must therefore be read as 'does the recipe survive on CPU', not as a GPU speed claim

the upstream kernel's edge behaviour is over-written by its own boundary-condition stage upstream; the comparison with a periodic reference is only meaningful after closing the wraps, which is exactly what A2 does

Taylor-Green compressibility error (O(Ma^2)) is a property of the D2Q9 BGK model, not of the streaming operator: the K3 error is expected to grow with u0 and shrink with L, and both trends are measured rather than assumed
